name: OP1177ARZ-REEL7
title: OP1177/OP2177/OP4177: precision, low-noise, low-bias-current op amps
summary: Bipolar precision op amps in single (OP1177), dual (OP2177) and quad (OP4177) versions, the fourth generation of the OP07 line. Offset is 15 µV typical (60 µV maximum, OP1177), drift 0.7 µV/°C maximum, bias current 2 nA maximum and noise 7.9 nV/√Hz, on about 400 µA per amplifier from ±2.5 V to ±15 V. Inputs carry 500 Ω series protection and tolerate signals beyond the supplies without phase reversal; the output drives 1000 pF unaided. OP1177ARZ-REEL7 is the single in 8-lead SOIC_N on a 7-inch reel.

circuits.title: Overload recovery test circuit
circuits.description: An inverting stage with a gain of −100 (R2/R1) driven by a 200 mV step, so the demanded output lies far past the supply and the output saturates; the 10 kΩ resistor is the load. The overvoltage recovery curves are taken in it.

circuits.title: Snubber for a large capacitive load
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower driving a load capacitance CL. A series RS-CS network from the output to ground damps the response; since RS sits outside the feedback loop, the output swing is not reduced. The snubber values for 10 nF, 50 nF and 200 nF loads are in the snubber table; with CL = 2 nF the test used RS = 200 Ω and CS = 0.47 µF.

circuits.title: Stray input capacitance
circuits.description: An inverting stage, R1 in and R2 in feedback, with Ct standing for the total capacitance at the inverting input (the inputs' own differential and common-mode capacitance plus the board's). Ct puts a zero in the noise gain that can erode phase margin.

circuits.title: Compensation with a feedback capacitor
circuits.description: The stray-capacitance stage with Cf across R2. Cf = (R1/R2) × Ct gives 90° of phase margin.

circuits.title: Capacitor between the inputs against EMI
circuits.description: An inverting stage with a capacitor C from the inverting input to the grounded noninverting input. Interference on one input is coupled onto the other, where the amplifier's CMRR rejects it; depending on its value, C can make the stage unstable.

circuits.title: Compensation with an input R-C network
circuits.description: The EMI capacitor with a resistor R in series. R raises the DC loop gain and so lowers the output error; placing the R-C break below the amplifier's second pole improves the phase margin. R is chosen from the R equation for a wanted phase margin, independently of C.

circuits.title: Difference amplifier
circuits.description: One amplifier with four resistors subtracts V1 from V2: with R4/R3 = R2/R1 the output is (R2/R1)(V2 − V1). The CMRR it reaches is set by how well the two ratios match, about 1/(2δ) for resistors of tolerance δ.

circuits.title: Type K thermocouple amplifier
circuits.description: An ADR293 reference feeds two dividers. R3 and diode D1 make a temperature-dependent voltage that, through R2 and R1, lifts the thermocouple's positive lead; R1, R2 and D1 sit in the isothermal block with the copper-to-thermocouple joints. R7, R6, the R5 trimmer and R4 set the noninverting input, R5 nulling the output. The negative lead reaches the inverting input through R8, with R9 at that input.

parts.note: trimming potentiometer, pins 1, 2 and wiper W

notes: R9 returns from the inverting input to ground at the V+ bypass capacitors; a feedback resistor would return to VOUT.
To compensate the cold junction, short the terminating junctions in the isothermal block with copper wire (a 0 °C point), trim R5 for zero output, then take the short away.

circuits.title: Low power linearized RTD amplifier
circuits.description: A 2.5 V ADR421 excites a bridge holding a 100 Ω RTD. Amplifier A holds the RTD's top at its grounded noninverting input and returns the bridge's lower arm to the RTD's far end. Amplifier B amplifies the bridge signal with 4.37 kΩ in series with 200 Ω (500 Ω adjustable across it) as feedback, and a share of its output, taken from a 5 kΩ potentiometer, returns to the RTD node through 49.9 kΩ. The adjustments set zero, full scale and linearity.
notes: Calibration: at the lowest temperature to be measured, adjust the zero rheostat for 0 V out. With the full-scale and linearity adjustments at mid-travel, apply 500 °C (or the RTD's resistance at 500 °C) and set full scale for 5 V; then at 250 °C set the linearity adjustment for 2.5 V. After this the error is within ±0.5 °C.

circuits.title: Single amplifier bridge
circuits.description: An ADR421 reference drives a four-arm bridge, one arm of value R(1 + δ) being the sensor. The two bridge midpoints go to the amplifier inputs, each with an RF: from the inverting side to the output and from the noninverting side to ground. One op amp takes the place of an instrumentation amplifier.

circuits.title: Two-stage band-pass KRC filter
circuits.description: Amplifier B, a follower, makes a second-order high-pass with C2, C1, R1 and R2; amplifier A, also a follower, makes a second-order low-pass with R3, R4, C3 and C4. Together they pass a band. The high-pass Q is set by R1/R2 (R1 = 20 kΩ, R2 = 10 kΩ); the low-pass Q by C3/C4.

circuits.title: Channel separation test circuit
circuits.description: Amplifier B, a follower, is driven with 50 mV; amplifier A has its noninverting input grounded and a gain set by 10 kΩ feedback over 100 Ω to ground. What appears at amplifier A's output measures the crosstalk from amplifier B.

operation.text: Single (OP1177), dual (OP2177) and quad (OP4177) precision bipolar op amps of the OP07 line: 60 µV maximum offset for the single, 0.7 µV/°C maximum drift, 2 nA maximum bias current, 8 nV/√Hz noise and about 400 µA per amplifier. All are specified over −40 °C to +125 °C, and the MSOP and TSSOP versions carry the same limits as the SOIC. The OP1177 and OP2177 come in 8-lead MSOP and SOIC_N; the OP4177 in 14-lead SOIC_N and TSSOP. MSOP and TSSOP are supplied on tape and reel only.
Runs from ±2.5 V to ±15 V (36 V absolute maximum across the supplies). Supply current stays under 500 µA per amplifier at 30 V total.

Unity-gain stable. Without any compensation it drives up to 1000 pF in any configuration; larger loads at unity gain need a snubber (RS in series with CS from output to ground). With CL = 2 nF the snubber cuts overshoot from 27 % to 5 % and removes the ringing. RS sits outside the feedback loop, so the snubber leaves the output swing intact; it does not restore the bandwidth that a large capacitive load costs.

Each input has 500 Ω in series inside, and the inputs survive 2.5 V beyond either supply with no harm. For more, add an external resistor that keeps the input current at or below 5 mA. With 5 kΩ in both inputs the added offset is under 5 µV (input offset current is below 1 nA), the noise is little changed, and the inputs withstand more than 27 V beyond either supply. The output does not reverse phase even with inputs past the supplies. Input offset rises by under 1 µV maximum for every 500 Ω of source resistance.

Settles to 0.01 % (1 mV) in about 45 µs after a 10 V step at noninverting unity gain. At ±15 V the output comes out of positive saturation in under 4 µs after more than 100 % overdrive, and out of negative saturation in 1.4 µs. For fast settling keep supply leads short and bypassed, use metal film resistors, and polystyrene or polycarbonate capacitors for low dielectric absorption.
THD + N is about 0.00025 % at unity gain, its worst configuration. Open-loop gain stays linear into heavy loads (RL = 2 kΩ), which keeps DC error and distortion low at high closed-loop gain.

Keep the board clean and dry; a coating limits moisture and leakage. Short supply traces with bypass capacitors right at the supply pins. Keep signal traces at least 5 mm from supply lines. Guard against thermocouple voltages at dissimilar-metal joints: orient resistors so heat reaches both ends alike, match the number and kind of parts in the two input paths (a zero-ohm resistor can balance a real one), place matched parts close together and alike, use equal lead lengths, and keep heat sources away from the input circuit. A ground plane is strongly advised; it cuts EMI and evens the board temperature.

Bias and offset currents change little with temperature, even at 125 °C. Low dissipation and stable behaviour over temperature keep warm-up drift small: the offset stays within ±0.2 µV of its value at turn-on over the first 120 s.
In the OP2177 the input and bias circuits are built to keep one channel's signal out of the other: better than −120 dB up to 100 kHz and better than −115 dB up to 1 MHz.

RTD self-heating can be 0.5 °C to 0.8 °C per mW. In the linearized RTD circuit the amplifier supply current is drawn through the bridge; even at the 600 µA maximum the RTD dissipates under 0.1 mW at its highest resistance, so the heating error stays under 0.1 °C.
